Five indemnities hand-computed from the CCIP Basic Provisions / CEPP rules (not the author's tests) all match: RP APH 200, 80%, P 4.00, H 5.00, 120 bu -> 160x5 - 120x5 = 200 (observed 200); YP APH 200, 75%, P 4, 100 bu -> 50 bu x 4 = 200 (200); RP with H 9.00 capped at 8.00, 100 bu -> 1280 - 800 = 480 (480); RP price fall H 3, 150 bu -> 640 - 450 = 190 (190). Whole default example recomputed by hand: expected net per acre 70% -2.62, 75% -0.70, 80% -0.88, 85% -7.36, best level 75%; break-even yields 124.67/132.96/140.78/147.24; all match. One edge: RP-HPE revenue to count uses the uncapped harvest price (calc.mjs:85; H 9 vs P 4, 50 bu gives 190 where a capped harvest price gives 240) - only bites when the harvest price is over 2x projected and yield under half the guarantee. Not 4: that edge and the silent input fallbacks.

The bolded output and half the cap rule are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (124 lines), index.html script (lines 122-155), usage.mjs. Clean pure module, escaped HTML output, no network. Defects: indemnityFor computes counted then re-branches on plan for the same value (calc.mjs:83-85, redundant); a blank or non-numeric numeric field silently becomes the default (index.html:128, it is at least written back into the field); '80, 1,200' parses the premium as $1 because the comma is the field separator (calc.mjs:48); APH 0 shows a negative break-even yield and price 0 prints 'NaN' (calc.mjs:110, index.html:140).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon; true), RP/HPE/YP definitions in the FAQ (match calc.mjs and the CCIP), 'does not pick one' (true, the best-expected-net line is caveated in place), disclaimer and no-warranty footer (index.html:116), defaults labelled placeholders (index.html:109), limits listed in README and the Not decided card. llms.txt source carries the github.io host but served-copy shows the deploy rewrites it (source-only, not filed). No unbacked claim found.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: farmer with an agent quote sheet for 70-85% RP wants to know if 85% is worth it over 80%. The tool gives the step cost ($11.70 extra premium for $41.40 extra guarantee, $0.283 per $1) and per-year nets, which is the real question. Gaps a practitioner hits in the first hour: expected values depend entirely on hand-typed years and chances (no county yield/price distribution, unlike farmdoc's premium calculator or the RMA Cost Estimator's loss estimates), no enterprise/optional unit, no SCO/ECO which is now the common add-on decision at 85%, and no whole-farm total beyond premium. Usable for a back-of-envelope comparison, not for the agent's recommendation.
evidence.domain: Method compared with FCIC Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions (revenue protection guarantee = APH x coverage x greater of projected/harvest price; YP and HPE at projected price) and the Commodity Exchange Price Provisions (harvest price limited to 200% of projected): RP guarantee and revenue to count follow them. Departure: RP-HPE revenue to count uses the uncapped harvest price (calc.mjs:84 comment says 'HPE has no uplift to cap'), whereas the CEPP harvest-price limit is in the harvest price definition itself (auditor reading; verify against the crop's CEPP). Unit structure, quality adjustment and appraised production are disclosed as not modelled. A practitioner would sign off on the per-acre arithmetic within the stated limits.

defects.what: The bolded 'level with the best expected net' is never asserted: inverting the sort so it names the worst level leaves all 21 tests green.

The 200% harvest-price limit on RP revenue to count is untested: the only cap test uses yield 0, so dropping the cap from revenue to count survives (it would overstate revenue and understate indemnity when the harvest price exceeds twice the projected price).

RP-HPE revenue to count uses the uncapped harvest price; under the Commodity Exchange Price Provisions the harvest price itself is limited to 200% of the projected price (auditor reading, verify against the crop's CEPP). APH 200, 80%, P 4, H 9, 50 bu gives 190 instead of 240.
A premium typed with a thousands separator ('80, 1,200') is read as $1 and not reported as skipped, because the comma doubles as the field separator.
APH 0 shows a negative break-even yield (-1.3 bu) and projected price 0 prints 'NaN' in the break-even column instead of a check-inputs message.
Coverage levels above the 85% offered for RP/YP individual coverage (e.g. 90, 100) are accepted silently.
No county yield/price distribution and no SCO/ECO or unit-structure option, so the expected-value view rests on hand-typed years; disclosed, but it is the gap an agent hits first.

verdict: A small, correct per-acre coverage-level comparator: every recomputed RP, YP and example output (5 hand calculations from the CCIP/CEPP rules plus the whole default example, best level 75% at -$0.70/acre) matched, claims are backed and the disclaimer and limits are in place. It misses the bar on verification: 3 of 5 seeded mutations survived, including the one that makes the bolded recommendation name the worst level and the one that drops the 200% cap from RP revenue to count. Fitness is 2 because expected values rest on typed scenarios with no county distribution, units or SCO/ECO. Small input-handling gaps and one probable RP-HPE harvest-price-cap departure.
